topics.name: Bias
topics.description: Higher-timeframe continuation versus reversal state that filters lower-timeframe execution.

topics.name: Candle 2 Closure
topics.description: Fractal-model closure concept used to interpret continuation and reversal development.

dependencies.rationale: The Candle 2 reversal is only useful when the surrounding directional idea is already framed.
Fractal reversals are intended to sit inside the higher-to-lower timeframe directional plan.
Large rejection wicks and midpoint respect help separate clean Candle 2 turns from weak ones.

topics.name: Candle 3 Closure
topics.description: Fractal-model continuation or reversal closure concept used for cleaner execution confirmation.

dependencies.rationale: Candle 3 only matters after Candle 2 failed to deliver the earlier closure.
Candle 3 refinement is explicitly framed through the midpoint of Candle 3's range.
Candle 3 closures are only promoted when they agree with the higher-timeframe point of interest and directional plan.

topics.name: Consolidation
topics.description: Smaller-range price behavior that often precedes expansion or reversal.

dependencies.rationale: Consolidation behaves differently depending on whether it is a pause or a transition.
Equilibrium helps classify whether price is still rotating inside the range or actually resolving away from it.
Manipulation and breakout confirmation rely on protected swing or candle-series failure structure.

topics.name: Continuation
topics.description: Execution logic for rejoining the active directional move after valid confirmation.

dependencies.rationale: Continuation trades only make sense in the direction of the active bias.
Candle 3 is repeatedly referenced as a cleaner continuation confirmation concept.
Equilibrium often separates shallow continuation pullbacks from deeper failure conditions.
Continuation is how traders participate in an ongoing expansion leg.
Protected swings define structural continuation entries and trailing logic.
Continuation quality rises when lower timeframe execution aligns with higher timeframe intent.

topics.name: Daily Profiles
topics.description: Session-shaped daily profile templates used to anticipate likely reversal, continuation, or range-expansion behavior.

dependencies.rationale: Daily profiles are specialized bias frameworks.
Profiles still need higher-to-lower timeframe continuity.
Profile interpretation uses wick and candle behavior extensively.

topics.name: Equilibrium
topics.description: Midpoint reference used for continuation framing and balance/imbalance logic.

topics.name: Expansion
topics.description: One-sided directional move with shallow pullbacks and continuation structure.

dependencies.rationale: Expansion execution quality depends on higher-timeframe continuation versus reversal context.
Protected swings define continuation structure and invalidation inside expansion.
TTrades expansion logic is explicitly multi-timeframe.
Wick behavior helps classify whether candles actually support expansion.

topics.name: Invalidation
topics.description: Structural failure conditions, stop placement, and thesis negation rules.

dependencies.rationale: Protected swings are the main structural stop and failure reference.
Invalidation often marks the shift from continuation to reversal.

topics.name: Protected Swings
topics.description: Structural highs or lows expected to hold if the current directional thesis remains valid.

topics.name: Retracement
topics.description: Countertrend pullback within a broader directional move.

dependencies.rationale: Retracement quality must be interpreted inside a broader directional thesis.
Retracement is defined in contrast to the prior expansion leg.
Retracement integrity and completion are judged against existing and newly formed protected swings.
Higher timeframe versus lower timeframe pullback structure matters for valid retracements.

topics.name: Reversal
topics.description: Phase transition where prior structure fails and opposite-direction structure confirms.

dependencies.rationale: Reversal setups need context to separate true reversals from simple pullbacks.
A reversal becomes cleaner once a new protected swing confirms in the opposite direction.
Reversals framed from daily or four-hour context are more reliable than lower-timeframe noise.
Wick behavior is a major TTrades signal for reversal versus expansion conditions.

topics.name: Top-Down Alignment
topics.description: Higher, intermediate, and lower timeframe agreement for directional precision.

topics.name: Wick Logic
topics.description: Use of wick size and opposing run behavior to classify expansion versus reversion potential.
